title: Comparison of Clinical and Radiological Results of Salter and Pemberton Osteotomy Surgery in Developmental Hip Dysplasia in Children
content: Background/Objectives: Salter and Pemberton osteotomies are used for acetabular reconstruction in children with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). We described outcomes after both procedures. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 50 children (67 operated hips) aged 18–72 months treated from 2017 to 2020: 47 hips underwent Salter osteotomy and 20 underwent Pemberton osteotomy. Because 17 children contributed bilateral hips and participant-level data were unavailable for cluster-adjusted reanalysis, outcomes were summarized descriptively. Results: Mean acetabular index decreased from 44.5 ± 9.9° to 19.0 ± 5.8° after Salter osteotomy and from 43.7 ± 7.5° to 21.5 ± 4.0° after Pemberton osteotomy. Modified McKay grades I–II were recorded in 72.3% and 80.0% of hips, respectively, and Severin grades I–II in 78.7% and 85.0%. Concomitant femoral osteotomy was performed in 17.0% and 50.0% of hips. The aggregate records listed three superficial infections and six postoperative fractures after Salter osteotomy and none after Pemberton osteotomy. Conclusions: Both groups showed substantial acetabular index reduction and mostly favorable clinical and radiographic grades. Nonrandom treatment selection, unequal follow-up, bilateral hips, and incomplete event detail preclude conclusions about equivalence, superiority, or comparative risk.
